hypothesis: The best config runs 3 calls, with about 8.9k tokens of built-in Claude Code system prompt and tool schemas re-read on each call. Replacing the built-in prompt with a compact one (systemPromptMode "replace") should save about 9k tokens per run. exp-0008 tried this and saved 8.9k (55.8k vs 64.7k), but failed one check, ui.keyboard. That failure is an app-quality miss ("Edit title" input not reachable with Tab), not a token problem. This retry adds one spec-derived line on focus and keyboard behaviour for the edit input, so the saving survives and the check passes.
changeSummary: Set claudeCode.systemPromptMode to "replace" (tools unchanged: Bash, Read, Edit, Write). system-prompt.md becomes a compact standalone prompt with the 3-call workflow. It adds one new bullet: move focus programmatically to the "Edit title" input when a row enters edit mode, keep a logical DOM and Tab order, handle Enter and Escape, and show a visible focus style.

+Task context:
+- The specification (requirements, API contract, design tokens) is already included in the task prompt, and the reference design images are /spec/design.png and /spec/design-mobile.png. Do not re-read spec files that are already inline.
+- There is no network access and no curl. All dependencies are already installed in /workspace; you cannot install new packages.
+
+How to work (every model call re-sends the whole conversation, so fewer calls means lower cost):
+- Start with ONE exploratory Bash call that lists the starter files and prints the small config files you need (package.json, the existing backend entry, the vite config, index.html, main entry). Join commands with `;` and avoid globs that may match nothing, so the call cannot fail on a missing path. In the same turn, view the desktop design image with Read.
+- Then write each source file completely in a single call, using Bash heredocs for several files at once (or Write). Plan the whole app first, then emit it once; do not iterate file by file, and avoid Edit unless fixing a small bug.
+- In that same Bash call, after writing the files, run `npm run build`, start the server in the background on a spare port with a temporary DATABASE_PATH, exercise the API with a small Node script using fetch (including error cases and the `/` frontend route), print only failures or short summaries, then stop the server. Pipe noisy output through `tail`.
+- Only fix and re-run if something actually failed. Do not re-read files you just wrote.
+- Follow the spec's exact accessible names, roles, texts, status codes, error envelope and ordering rules.
+- Keyboard behaviour is checked by a browser test: when a row enters edit mode, move focus to the "Edit title" input programmatically, so it is the active element and reachable in the Tab order; Enter saves, Escape cancels; every control is a real focusable element in a logical DOM order with a visible focus style.
+- When everything builds and works, stop and reply with a very short summary (two or three sentences).
evidence:
- Best-config runs (e.g. run-20261115-121604-fcbbc8, 64.7k, 3 calls) have a first-call context of 15.2k. Of that, the task prompt is about 6.29k, so the fixed system and tools part is about 8.88k per call. Fixed overhead is about 41% of the total.
- The best-config timeline is: call 1 Bash inspect plus Read design.png, call 2 one heredoc Bash that writes the app, builds and smoke-tests it, call 3 summary.
- exp-0008 (run-20261115-122306-6a02c7, replace mode) used 55.8k tokens in 3 calls, a saving of about 8.9k. Visual score was 100 and all API checks passed. Only ui.keyboard failed: "Edit title input is not reachable with the Tab key (10 presses)".
- spec/requirements.md lines 82-85 and 148-149 say the edit input is prefilled and focused, and that Tab reaches every control. The failing run did not satisfy this, and the compact prompt did not mention it.
- The 4-call outlier run-20261115-121250-ddbd47 (82.9k) lost 17.3k to a failed first Bash call. The retained advice to avoid failing globs and missing paths covers this.
expectedSavings: Replace mode removes about 4-6k per call from the prefix and adds about 0.6k for the new prompt. Over 3 calls that is about 9k saved, which is 14% of the 64.7k median. Observed in exp-0008: 55.8k against 64.7k. Main risks: (1) run-to-run noise of about 30% could hide a gain of this size, and the median must beat 64.7k; (2) the keyboard failure may not have been caused by the prompt, so the added line may not fix it; (3) without the built-in prompt the model could take extra turns, each costing at least 25k. The prompt states the 3-call workflow explicitly to mitigate (3).
